title: Apply forward force from one leg and organize the receiving leg.
brief: The forward same-leg hop is the priority. Low unilateral ankle contacts, an opposite-leg bound, a supported-height takeoff and a small vertical one-leg jump separate the propulsion and receiving tasks; a staggered throw rehearses force from an unequal base without another landing.

explosive.name: Forward Hop to Stick — Same Leg
explosive.job: Own a single-leg forward push and receive on that same leg.
explosive.cue: Use one comfortable dip and natural arms, hop forward, absorb through ankle/knee/hip and hold the same-foot landing 2 s.
explosive.regress: Shorten travel; stop for repeated free-foot touchdown, knee collapse or painful contact.

explosive.name: Single-Leg Pogo in Place
explosive.job: Supply a small ankle-rebound dose on each support leg without long travel.
explosive.cue: Keep a softly bent knee and make low same-foot rebounds in place; settle after the third.
explosive.regress: Reduce height; stop for stiff painful contacts or uncontrolled travel.
explosive.intent: Low amplitude and quick, not maximum height

explosive.name: Opposite-leg Forward Bound to Stick
explosive.job: Transfer forward impulse from a pushing leg to a different receiving leg.
explosive.cue: Push from one foot, swing the opposite thigh forward and land on that opposite foot; hold 2 s.
explosive.regress: Shorten the bound and reduce free-leg swing; stop if reaching the landing foot causes a collapse.

explosive.name: Sprinter Step-Up Jump — Two-foot Floor Landing
explosive.job: Drive through a forward supported stance leg while coordinating the free knee.
explosive.cue: Start with one entire foot on a very low stable step, drive up/forward from that leg and land on both feet on the clear floor; hold 2 s and walk to reset.
explosive.regress: Use a lower step and smaller flight; stop if the rear foot pushes off or the floor landing becomes a drop the athlete cannot control.
explosive.gate: Suitable low step and familiar jump-off/floor landing.

explosive.name: Split-Stance Forward Medicine Ball Scoop Toss
explosive.job: Coordinate forward release from a staggered support base without a landing.
explosive.cue: Hold the lead-foot stance fixed, dip shallowly and extend through the legs into a forward two-hand scoop; no trunk rotation or step.
explosive.regress: Use a lighter ball and smaller dip; stop if the rear foot slips or the throw becomes a twist.
explosive.intent: Fast release with a light ball; retain the prescribed grounded support

explosive.name: Single-leg Vertical Jump to Two-foot Landing
explosive.job: Express stance-leg extension without the added forward braking of E1.
explosive.cue: Dip on one leg, jump a modest height with natural arms, bring both feet into a quiet two-foot landing and hold 2 s.
explosive.regress: Reduce height; stop if takeoff knee/pelvis control is lost.

control.name: Hip Airplane Iso Hold — Hand Supported
control.job: Lightly control hip/pelvis rotation around the planted leg for a forward landing.
control.cue: Hinge shallowly on one leg with stable hand support; open the pelvis slightly and hold without rotating the stance knee or foot.
control.regress: Reduce hinge/rotation; stop if balance or hamstring tension dominates.
control.intent: Bodyweight/light resistance, easy control; at least 5 clean reps in reserve or comparable ease

control.name: Self-resisted Seated Ankle Dorsiflexion
control.job: Strengthen controlled toe lift for foot placement and early heel acceptance.
control.cue: Sit with the heel planted; press lightly downward on the top of the forefoot with the hand while the foot lifts against it, then return slowly.
control.regress: Reduce hand resistance; keep toes relaxed and stop on discomfort.
control.intent: Bodyweight/light resistance, easy control; at least 5 clean reps in reserve or comparable ease

strength.name: Hip Thrust — pelvic dumbbell, upper back on bench
Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated, dumbbells on thighs

decision: Unilateral landing contacts are introduced only for athletes with actual competence. The static-start class does not grant that competence. Low pogo contacts are limited to three per leg; the main hop has eight attempts while the step-up and vertical supports use two per leg. Strength priority shifts to split squat (two sets per side); squat falls to two sets and walkout to three cycles to constrain combined unilateral/posterior-chain fatigue. Loads are held at current demonstrated capacity.
next_job: Class 4 will link arm timing with a staggered bilateral takeoff; review response to single-leg contacts before any new exposure.
